To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the growth of h-BN thin film from the ammonia-borane precursor is strongly affected by the background pressure.

the growth rate of hexagonal boron-nitride (h-BNN) thin films from ammonia-borane is increased and the resulting films are more disordered and amorphous when the total pressure is greater than 2.0Torr and the precursor flux exceeds the background pressure at the start of the growth.

the growth rate and crystallinity of hexagonal boron-nitride (h-Bn) films grown by chemical vapor deposition (cvd) are strongly dependent on the background pressure of Ar/H2 and on the partial pressure of H3N–Bh3 precursor, and that the growth rate increases as the background pressure increases, but the h-Bn becomes more amorphous and sp3-boned.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of total pressure on the growth of hexagonal boron-nitride (h-Bn) films from the precursor ammonia borane.
the synthesis of high-quality, large-area h-BN films using a single-source precursor.
the role of the total background pressure during CVD of h-BN thin film growth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the growth rate of h-BN films using the H3–N–BH3 is limited by the precursor partial pressure and not PTOT.
the growth of h-BN using the H3BNBH3 precursor is sensitive to PTOT and the partial pressure of H3N–B3H3, and that the growth rate of h-BN can be controlled by varying these parameters.
the total pressure of the background gas is a key parameter in controlling the quality and properties of h-BN thin film growth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
h-BN thin film growth using the H2N–BH3 as precursor is a promising approach for large-area growth of high-quality h-BN films.
the use of H3N–B3H3 precursor is a promising route to grow h-BN thin film with high quality.
the growth rate of h-BN is proportional to the partial pressure of the precursor and inversely proportional to PTOT.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the total pressure during growth of h-BN thin film from H3N–BN3 precursor can be a key factor to control the crystalline quality of h-BN films.
the background pressure PTOTO has a strong effect on the growth of h-BN from H3N–B3, which is a promising precursor for h-BN growth.
, in order to grow high quality h-BN, one must ensure that the total pressure in the CVD reactor is kept low.
